package_info.package_versions: Malicious versions published after May 15, 2022 (exact versions not specified)
package_info.why_malicious: The package was compromised via a maintainer account takeover and injected with code that, upon import, exfiltrates all environment variables to an attacker-controlled server. This results in the theft of credentials, secrets, and other sensitive data from any environment where the package is imported.

execution_context.file_location: core package module (likely __init__.py or main module, executes immediately upon import; exact file not specified in report)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At import-time, the code imports the os and requests modules, collects all environment variables from the running process, and sends them via HTTP POST to a hardcoded attacker-controlled Heroku domain, resulting in exfiltration of sensitive data and credentials.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The code transmits the entire set of environment variables to an external server without user consent or legitimate purpose, which is a clear indicator of credential theft and data exfiltration.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate Python packages do not access and transmit all environment variables to external servers, especially not automatically at import-time. Such behavior is highly abnormal and violates user trust and security best practices.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Some legitimate packages may send limited, non-sensitive telemetry or error data, but they never transmit full environment variables or secrets, and always provide user notification or opt-in mechanisms.
key_indicators: Automatic HTTP POST to external domain during import
Bulk access and exfiltration of environment variables via os.environ
Use of hardcoded attacker-controlled Heroku domain (anti-theft-web.herokuapp.com)
Network activity initiated from package initialization code

attack_chain.action: Attacker compromises the original maintainer's PyPI account and uploads a new malicious version of the ctx package containing the exfiltration code.
attack_chain.leads_to: Malicious code is distributed to users via PyPI.

attack_chain.action: User installs or upgrades to the compromised ctx package from PyPI.
attack_chain.leads_to: Malicious code is present in the user's environment.

attack_chain.action: When the ctx package is imported in a Python process, the malicious code executes, harvesting all environment variables from the process.
attack_chain.leads_to: Sensitive data, including credentials and secrets, is collected from the environment.

attack_chain.action: The harvested environment variables are exfiltrated via HTTP POST to the attacker's Heroku app (anti-theft-web.herokuapp.com).
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker gains unauthorized access to secrets, credentials, and other sensitive information from affected systems.

behavioral_signatures: Network requests initiated at import-time by Python packages
Bulk access to environment variables (os.environ) in package initialization code
HTTP POST requests containing environment data to external domains
file_indicators: Presence of code importing both os and requests modules and posting os.environ data
Unexpected network communication code in __init__.py or main module files of third-party packages
network_indicators: Outbound HTTP POST requests to anti-theft-web.herokuapp.com
Unusual network activity from Python processes during package import or initialization
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for Python packages that initiate network requests at import-time, especially those sending environment variables. Flag any HTTP POST requests to suspicious domains such as anti-theft-web.herokuapp.com originating from package initialization code. Use static analysis to detect code patterns that access os.environ and transmit its contents externally. Correlate installation or import of the ctx package with unexpected outbound network activity.
